content.title: Silver Price Tumbles 14%, Gold Down 7% Amid Inflation Fears
content.text: ToplineGold and silver faced a steep selloff Thursday morning, with the price of gold falling about 7% and silver tumbling 14% as both metals continue a losing streak as inflationary risks amid the Iran war lower the prospect of interest rate cuts.Gold and silver prices sank to a more than one-month low Thursday. (Photo by Sven Hoppe/picture alliance via Getty Images)dpa/picture alliance via Getty ImagesKey FactsSilver futures are down 14% as of 9 a.m. EST Thursday, with the metal hitting a low of about $66.50, while spot silver is also down 12%.The price of gold is about $4,550 as of 9 a.m., down about 7%.Gold and silver prices are at their lowest levels since early February, as the prices of both metals have consistently declined throughout the war in Iran. Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo ​Bank, told Reuters metals prices are falling amid a “stronger dollar and a more hawkish tone from Fed ​Chair Jerome Powell following the latest FOMC meeting,” citing Powell’s warning that high energy prices will push up inflation as the central bank held interest rates steady. Surging oil prices amid the Iran war and inflationary fears are “weighing on gold,” ING analysts told the Wall Street Journal.Why Isn’t The Iran War Lifting Metals Prices?Gold and silver prices have consistently trended downward since the United States and Israel began striking Iran nearly three weeks ago, bucking conventional wisdom that global conflict makes the price of “safe haven” assets—like precious metals—rise. Analysts from Sucden Financial said Wednesday gold and silver are trading “in negative correlation with oil” as oil and energy prices surge. The analysts said “bullion may find some support from geopolitical uncertainty, but as long as oil absorbs the main safe-haven bid, upside will likely remain constrained.” Oil prices have been on the rise for weeks, and the Brent crude oil benchmark surged early Thursday, briefly hitting a high of $119 after Iranian strikes on energy facilities in Qatar caused “extensive damage.” The rising energy costs have stoked inflationary fears, and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said Wednesday the central bank would keep interest rates unchanged, putting downward pressure on metals. The dollar has also strengthened in recent weeks, which also typically has an inverse correlation with metals prices. Key BackgroundGold and silver prices are still up significantly year-over-year, but they have fallen far from highs they reached in January before their historic price rally came to a halt. At their peaks earlier this year, gold prices rose about $5,600 and silver prices topped $120. Prices came crashing down once President Donald Trump named Kevin Warsh as his pick to lead the Federal Reserve, as Warsh was considered less likely to slash interest rates.
